name: Ethical Purchasing Group - SIA Project 22 23
description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS),
    known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a
    km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect
    groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a
    conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality,
    characteristics, availability, and price.

    The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis.
    Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday
    at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify
    the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop
    characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

    The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing
    descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the
    minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability
    entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

    Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place
    orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers
    are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of
    people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an
    order.

    Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by
    store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed,
    the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order
    constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met,
    the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an
    order summary to the customer by email.

    Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm
    the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available
    quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed.
    When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies
    precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable
    quantities from lower-priority orders.

    Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a
    modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers.
    If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

    After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically
    performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order.
    Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each
    customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

    If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order
    placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains
    valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed,
    the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the
    wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order
    is cancelled.

    Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time
    slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view
    the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages
    corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee
    confirms the collection of the order.

    If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system
    sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the
    order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

    Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store
    employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods
    have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder.
    If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer
    orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected
    customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are
    informed of the delivery problem.

    The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents
    the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used
    as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient.
    The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received,
    forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores
    are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities
    must be allocated among competing orders.

highLevelGoals: Farmers aim to efficiently submit estimates of available products, including type, quantity, price, and characteristics, to the system.
Farmers seek to confirm the final quantities of products they can supply to ensure accurate order processing and fulfillment.
Farmers aim to deliver their products to the store within the specified timeframe to facilitate subsequent customer pickups.
Customers aim to easily browse available products from local farmers, understand their characteristics, and place orders for desired quantities.
Customers seek to have their orders processed correctly, receive notifications about any modifications due to availability, and confirm final order details.
Customers aim to maintain a sufficient balance in their virtual wallet for automatic payments and be informed of any payment-related issues.
Customers desire the ability to schedule a pickup time and confirm the collection of their orders from the store.
Customers aim to uphold a positive fair-play score to ensure priority in order allocation and demonstrate their reliability within the purchasing group.
Store employees aim to assist customers with order placement, modifications, and ensure all order details are accurately managed within the system.
Store employees seek to manage customer virtual wallet recharges and resolve payment issues to ensure smooth and successful transactions.
Store employees aim to efficiently manage the pickup schedule, prepare customer orders, and confirm successful collection of goods.
Store employees aim to confirm the receipt of products from farmers, track delivery status, and manage any discrepancies or delays.
lowLevelGoals: Farmer can submit an estimate of available products, including type, estimated quantity, price per unit, and specific characteristics, to the system.
Farmer can update an existing product estimate with revised estimated quantity, price per unit, or characteristics.
Farmer can retrieve and review a list of all their currently submitted product estimates.
Farmer can confirm the final actual quantity for a specific product estimate they can supply.
Farmer can view a list of all products for which they have confirmed actual quantities.
Farmer can report a discrepancy between the confirmed quantity and the actual quantity available for delivery.
Farmer can mark a specific product delivery as dispatched from their farm.
Farmer can view the scheduled delivery times for their products to the store.
Farmer can report an anticipated delay in product delivery and provide an updated estimated arrival time.
Customer can browse a list of available products, optionally filtering by product type, farmer, or price range.
Customer can view detailed information for a specific product, including its characteristics, origin, and farmer information.
Customer can add a specified quantity of a product to their shopping cart.
Customer can place an order for all items currently in their shopping cart.
Customer can view the current details of their active orders, including items, quantities, and total price.
Customer can receive a notification if their order has been modified due to product availability or other reasons.
Customer can confirm the final details of their order after any modifications have been applied.
Customer can cancel an order before it reaches a certain processing stage.
Customer can view their current virtual wallet balance.
Customer can initiate a recharge of their virtual wallet using a specified payment method and amount.
Customer can receive an alert when their virtual wallet balance falls below a predefined threshold.
Customer can view a history of all transactions made from and to their virtual wallet.
Customer can select and schedule a preferred pickup time for their order from available time slots.
Customer can view the details of their scheduled order pickup, including time and location.
Customer can confirm the successful collection of their order from the store.
Customer can receive a reminder notification for an upcoming order pickup.
Customer can view their current fair-play score.
Customer can receive a notification when their fair-play score is updated (e.g., after an order cancellation or successful pickup).
Customer can access information explaining how the fair-play score is calculated and its implications.
Store Employee can search for customer orders using criteria such as customer ID, order ID, or order status.
Store Employee can assist a customer by adding items to their cart and initiating an order on their behalf.
Store Employee can modify an existing customer order, such as adjusting quantities or removing items, on behalf of the customer.
Store Employee can view the complete order history for a specific customer.
Store Employee can process a recharge for a customer's virtual wallet, specifying the amount and payment method.
Store Employee can view the virtual wallet balance for a specific customer.
Store Employee can manually resolve a payment issue for a customer, such as marking an order as paid or adjusting a balance.
Store Employee can generate a report detailing payment transactions for a specified period or customer.
Store Employee can view the schedule of all customer order pickups for the current day.
Store Employee can mark a specific customer order as prepared and ready for pickup.
Store Employee can confirm that a customer has successfully collected their order.
Store Employee can reschedule a customer's pickup time for an order if requested or necessary.
Store Employee can view a list of all expected incoming product deliveries from farmers.
Store Employee can confirm the receipt of a farmer's delivery, including recording actual quantities received.
Store Employee can report any discrepancies found in a farmer's delivery, such as quantity mismatches or damaged goods.
Store Employee can update the status of a farmer's delivery (e.g., 'received', 'partially received', 'delayed').

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors (Farmer, Customer, Store Employee) are correct and cover all the active entities described in the system. However, the description mentions that "Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people." While the system interacts with the representative, the "Purchasing Group" (or GAS) is a distinct entity in the domain that holds the collective order and fair-play score context. In GORE, it is often beneficial to explicitly identify the "Purchasing Group Representative" or acknowledge the group as a stakeholder/actor context to distinguish from individual customers in other systems. More importantly, the description states that "Store employees can enter orders... on behalf of customers." This confirms the Store Employee role. The main potential omission is the explicit distinction of the "Purchasing Group" as an actor or the specific role of the "Group Representative" if the system treats the group as a first-class citizen for data (e.g., group-level fair play or orders). Given the description says "only the registered representative of each group can submit an order," the actor is effectively the Representative. The current label "Customer" is acceptable but slightly generic. A more precise label might be "Group Representative" or "Customer Representative". However, "Customer" is not incorrect. The score is high because the core actors are present and correctly described.

branch_001.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the full lifecycle of managing product estimates by a farmer, encompassing the creation, modification, and retrieval of their submitted product availability information within the system.

branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively enable the farmer to confirm, track, and adjust the actual quantities of products they commit to supply, thereby ensuring comprehensive management of their supply commitments.

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Farmer can manage product delivery status and schedule
branch_003.rationale: These operations collectively enable the farmer to monitor scheduled deliveries, confirm their dispatch, and proactively report any delays, thereby providing comprehensive control and communication over the product delivery process from the farm to the store.

branch_004.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for a customer to find, evaluate, select, and ultimately acquire products. Browsing and viewing details facilitate product discovery and evaluation, adding to the cart enables selection, and placing an order completes the transaction. All these operations are sequential and integral steps in the customer's journey to purchase products.

branch_005.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Customer Management and Control of Active Orders
branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide customers with comprehensive capabilities to monitor, react to changes in, and exert control over their orders after placement but before final fulfillment. This includes viewing details, being informed of modifications, confirming changes, and having the option to cancel.

branch_006.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Customer to Manage Their Virtual Wallet
branch_006.rationale: The low-level goals collectively provide the customer with comprehensive capabilities to oversee, control, and maintain the funds within their virtual wallet. This includes monitoring the current balance, reviewing past transactions, receiving proactive alerts, and initiating recharges, all of which are essential aspects of effective virtual wallet management.

branch_007.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of a customer's interaction with an order pickup, encompassing scheduling, viewing details, receiving reminders, and confirming collection. They all contribute to ensuring a smooth and informed customer experience for order pickups.

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide Transparency and Understanding of Customer Fair-Play Score
branch_008.rationale: These low-level goals collectively aim to ensure that customers have complete visibility into their fair-play score, are informed of any changes, and fully understand how it is calculated and its implications. This holistic approach fosters transparency and empowers customers with knowledge about their standing.

branch_009.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Store Employee to provide comprehensive customer order support.
branch_009.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the capabilities a Store Employee needs to assist customers with their orders. They cover the full lifecycle of customer order interaction, including searching for existing orders, initiating new ones, modifying current orders, and reviewing past order history. All operations are performed on behalf of the customer to provide complete support.

branch_010.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Customer Virtual Wallet and Payment Operations
branch_010.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the capabilities a Store Employee needs to effectively handle all aspects of customer virtual wallets and their associated payment transactions. This includes adding funds, monitoring balances, resolving discrepancies, and reporting on activities, all of which fall under the umbrella of managing these operations.

branch_011.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the various actions a store employee performs to oversee, prepare, and complete the process of customers collecting their orders, including handling scheduling adjustments. They all contribute to the efficient and accurate management of the order pickup workflow.

1. **Farmer**: 'Provide product availability and details' covers the initial estimation; 'Confirm actual product quantities' covers the Monday confirmation; 'Ensure timely product delivery to the store' covers the Tuesday delivery obligation.
2. **Customer**: 'Discover and order local produce' covers browsing and ordering; 'Ensure order accuracy and fulfillment' covers handling modifications/cancellations; 'Manage personal payment for purchases' covers wallet management and payment issues; 'Conveniently collect purchased goods' covers scheduling and pickup; 'Maintain a reliable purchasing record' covers the fair-play score aspect.
3. **Store Employee**: 'Support customer order management' covers entering orders on behalf of customers; 'Oversee customer payment processes' covers wallet recharges; 'Coordinate product pickup logistics' covers preparing packages and confirming collection; 'Verify farmer deliveries' covers confirming receipt and handling delivery delays/discrepancies.

There are no distinct actor-level functional intentions in the description that are not already captured by these broad goals. The system's automated actions (like sending SMS reminders or updating fair-play scores) are consequences of the actors' actions or system states managed under these existing goals, rather than separate high-level goals for the actors themselves.

branch_002.rationale: Both low-level goals enable the farmer to interact with and oversee the quantities of products they are committed to supplying for orders. One facilitates the submission of new commitments, while the other allows for the review of existing ones, collectively supporting the management of their supply obligations.

branch_002.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Confirm actual product quantities' accurately captures the specific functional intention of the Farmer described in the project documentation: 'Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning.' This is a distinct phase from the initial estimation ('Provide product availability and details') and the physical delivery ('Ensure timely product delivery to the store'). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Farmer's Product Supply Commitments' is too generic and overlaps significantly with the existing HLG 'Provide product availability and details', as both deal with the farmer's supply obligations. The original goal is more precise and faithful to the specific action of confirming final quantities to trigger order processing. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The parent HLG 'Confirm actual product quantities' is supported by the documentation stating that 'Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning.' The current LLGs cover the two essential aspects of this interaction: submitting the confirmation (llg_001) and reviewing the confirmed state (llg_002). The documentation does not specify any other distinct capabilities for the farmer in this phase (e.g., editing after confirmation is not mentioned, and the system handles the allocation logic automatically). The sibling HLG 'Provide product availability and details' covers the initial estimation phase, which is distinct from the final confirmation. Therefore, the decomposition is complete and accurate.
